summary.short: Ohio policy binding state agencies, boards and commissions under the Governor on AI use planning, procurement, security, privacy and governance. Requires use-case approval, human verification of consequential AI outputs, supplier and generative AI controls, and an AI Council. No effective date stated.
summary.long: Sets statewide requirements for planning, procurement, security, privacy and governance of AI use by Ohio state agencies, boards and commissions under the Governor, citing ORC 125.18 as authority. Agencies must approve AI use cases, document testing, and keep human review for AI outputs and for decisions with legal or financial impact. Procurement rules cover supplier disclosure of generative AI, documentation of AI systems, a bar on supplier use of state data in generative AI absent approval, and licensing due diligence for training data. Workforce rules require approval for generative AI use, disclosure of generative AI-created deliverables, and entry of only public-record data into such tools. Security and privacy controls include risk assessment, a bar on sensitive data in unconstrained generative AI tools, consent before AI systems collect PII, and disclosure to users that they are interacting with a state AI solution. A multi-agency AI Council under DAS oversees a statewide sandbox and auditing of AI solutions. The policy is to be reviewed at least every two years. The text states no penalties and no effective date.

relations.note: Cited as the policy's authority. The text gives no further detail on the power relied on.
Defines Confidential Personal Information by reference to Section 1347.15 of the Ohio Revised Code, which sets its scope.

Internal inconsistency: Section III.F limits the AI Council's remit to Generative AI solutions, while III.A.2 and III.C.2.b send AI use cases and all new AI software to the Council. The Authority section cites only 'ORC 125.18' without a title or text. Footnotes were omitted from the source text.

events.note: No adoption, signature, publication, entry-into-force or application dates appear in the document. The only time-related provision is a recurring review requirement ('reviewed no less than every two years and updated as needed', Section VIII), which is a procedural review cycle with no stated legal consequence and is not coded as an event.

thresholds.note: The policy text contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. The only time period, the two-year review cycle in Section VIII, is a procedural limit and is recorded as an event rather than a threshold. Citations, addresses and phone numbers are not thresholds.
